SEC Announces Enforcement Results for Fiscal Year 2026

Published 2026-10-05 09:30 UTC

The Securities and Exchange Commission today announced enforcement results for fiscal year 2026, reporting that it filed 612 enforcement actions and obtained orders for $4.1 billion in financial remedies, including disgorgement, prejudgment interest and civil penalties.

Of the actions filed, 398 were standalone actions brought in federal court or as administrative proceedings, while the remainder were follow-on proceedings or actions against delinquent filers. The SEC distributed $780 million to harmed investors during the year through its fair funds and disgorgement programs.

Key areas of focus included offering frauds targeting retail investors, insider trading, accounting and disclosure violations, and misconduct by investment advisers. The SEC brought a number of cases involving crypto asset platforms and promoters, as well as actions against firms that failed to preserve business communications sent through personal messaging apps.

The Division of Enforcement also highlighted the work of its whistleblower program, which received more than 18,000 tips during the year. The SEC awarded approximately $230 million to whistleblowers whose information led to successful enforcement actions.

The SEC barred 129 individuals from serving as officers and directors of public companies or from working in the securities industry. The agency said such bars are among its most important tools for protecting investors from repeat offenders.

The Director of the Division of Enforcement thanked staff for their work and said the agency will continue to prioritize cases that protect retail investors and hold individuals accountable. A detailed report with statistics by case type is available on the SEC's website.

The agency also noted that it continued to work closely with criminal authorities, and that parallel criminal charges were filed in many of its most significant cases. Detailed statistics on enforcement actions by category will be included in the agency's annual report to Congress.
